utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, please call the case -- oh, Mr. Registrar. I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case IT-04-84bis-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj, Idriz Balaj, and Lahi Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Could we have appearances for the day, starting with the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: For the Prosecution, Aditya Menon, Daniela Kravetz, Barbara Goy, with our case manager, Line Pedersen. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. And could we have for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: For Mr. Haradinaj, Ben Emmerson, Rod Dixon, Annie O'Reilly, and Andrew Strong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Emmerson. And for Mr. Balaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Gregor Guy-Smith, Colleen Rohan, Chad Mair on behalf of Mr. Balaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Guy-Smith. Yes, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Brahimaj, Richard Harvey, Paul Troop, and assisted for the last time by our case manager, Sophie Rigney, who sadly leaves us today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Mr. Menon, we were still arguing your page and I guess the parties have finished now. The Chamber can rule?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Objection overruled. Carry on, Mr. Menon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution calls Bislim Zyrapi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Zyrapi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Mr. Zyrapi, just to remind you that you're still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony yesterday to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Yes, Mr. Menon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could call up 65 ter exhibit number 03002. And if the witness could just be shown the Albanian version. And if we could go to -- excuse me, Your Honour, if we could -- I jumped ahead of myself. If we could go to Exhibit P160, admitted Exhibit P160 and if the witness could just be shown the Albanian version and if the English and Albanian versions could be shown to the court. If we could go to page 9 of the English version and page 12 of the Albanian version. I think we're still on the wrong exhibit, actually. P160, admitted Exhibit P160 -- or, we're on the wrong page, excuse me. So page 9 of the English version and page 12 of the Albanian version. I see in front of me page 9 of the Albanian version. What I need is page 12 of the -- oh, excuse me, page 9 -- I'm sorry, Your Honour. Page 9 of the English version and page 12 of the Albanian version. I had it the wrong way around. And only the Albanian version for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, do you see paragraph 46 in front of you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Can you read that paragraph to yourself, and when you get to the end of that can you let us know so that we can scroll to the next page of the Albanian version.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Could we scroll to the next page of the Albanian version, page 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Can you read the remaining part of that paragraph, sir.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, there's a reference to a book in this particular paragraph. Can you tell us what that book is called.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The title of this book is: "Dialogue with Commander Ramush Haradinaj."

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And now can we call up --

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And I just want you to remember what has been said in this particular paragraph that you read to yourself, sir. Keep that in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Can we call up 65 ter 03002 and for the time being can we stay on the first page of the Albanian and English versions and obviously just the Albanian version for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, can you read out the title of this book.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: "A Narrative About War and Freedom."

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And what else?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: And below is "Dialogue with Commander Ramush Haradinaj."

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And now can we go to page 138 in the English version and page 132 in the Albanian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, do you see that there's a question on that page in the Albanian version. I'd like you to read everything under the question. And when we get to the -- when you get to the end of that page can you let us know so we can scroll to the next page.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Can we scroll to the next page of the English and the Albanian versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And can you read that page to yourself, sir.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us when you say in your statement at paragraph 46 that: "At a later meeting of members of the General Staff including me and Ramush during August/September 1998 we discussed logistics problems. More details about what was discussed with Ramush can be found at pages 134 to 138 of the book entitled 'A Narrative about War and Freedom: Dialogue with Commander Ramush Haradinaj.'" When you said that in your statement, sir, were you referring to the excerpt you just read?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said in my statement. I gave details about the reasons and so on, but the book has a number of other details which were not known to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And can you tell us why they are not known to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think stay on the topics.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Well, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The topic is this page. It's not other details.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understood the witness to say that in these pages there were other details that were not known to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Fair enough. I will rephrase the question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We probably mis -- heard different things.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Perhaps we might ask Mr. Menon to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Well, I was about to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Can I sir -- sir, you referred to a meeting in your statement in August/September 1998. And when you say there are more details about what was discussed at that meeting, are those details captured within the excerpt you've read? I'm only interested in the meeting, sir.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, during the meeting we discussed logistic problems which are reflected here, the logistics from Albania, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And when you say they're reflected here, are you referring to the document in front of you marked 65 ter 03002?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to have the two pages which the witness has read, so that would be pages 132 to 133 of the Albanian version and pages 138, I believe, to 139 of the English version of this particular exhibit admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, could Your Honours defer that decision until after cross-examination so that we can clarify exactly which passages within those pages the witness is able independently to verify?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think you can cross-examine on those passages that you don't want to have -- that you don't believe -- I don't see how we can defer this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours don't need to admit the exhibit until the end of the witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can be heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Menon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I think the basis for admissibility has been established. The witness -- the basis is a prima facie showing of reliability, and I think the witness has established that he's indicated -- he's made a statement in his 92 ter -- he's made an assertion in his 92 ter statement about a meeting that he participated with Ramush Haradinaj and he's indicated that details about that particular meeting are reflected indeed the text which he's read in this particular book. And so there is the basis for admission and I see no reason to postpone that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Menon. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the relevant pages of 65 ter number 03002 will be Exhibit P283, and, Your Honours, if counsel can notify the Registry when those pages are uploaded in the e-court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, I'd just like to change the topic here and I'd like to move on to your visit to the Dukagjin zone in mid-July 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And if we could pull up P159 and go to e-court page 41.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Now, sir, in your evidence -- if we could just enlarge the page a bit so it's a little bigger.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, for reference I'm alluding to lines 8 and 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, in your prior testimony in the Haradinaj case you indicated that you had met Ramush Haradinaj in Jabllanice in mid-July 1998, and you refer to a meeting that was held, a meeting between the General Staff of the KLA and Ramush Haradinaj. Can you tell us, sir, what was discussed at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the meeting at Jabllanice was held in mid-July 1998 and it was a meeting between the General Staff and the commander of the operative zone of Dukagjin. We discussed problems which were pertinent at the time, ways of co-ordinating the work of the operative zone and the General Staff as well as other zones. We discussed questions of supply or logistics as well. If I recall correctly, this was the array of issues we discussed at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And when you say "we discussed ways of co-ordinating the work of the operative zone and the General Staff as well as other zones," can you elaborate on that. What did that co-ordination relate to, sir?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I mentioned co-ordination, you have to remember that it was the time to improve the co-ordination of work between the operative zones and between the zones and the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: But what was the co-ordination about? What were you trying to co-ordinate, sir ?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I say co-ordination between the zones and the General Staff, was that there were a number of local units which were outside the command structures and they needed to be unified and co-opted into these zone of commands so that the zones and the staffs would co-ordinate their work better between themselves as well as between these operative zones and the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, when you said that "we discussed questions of supply or logistics," are you able to elaborate on that as well?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the issue of logistics and the supply, the issue was that the main supply route came from Albania via the operative zone of Dukagjin and on the way to other zones, so that we wanted to co-ordinate this passage towards the other zones, given that the main zone responsible for it was the Dukagjin zone. So they had the responsibility to -- way to welcome these supplies and to make sure that they were transited towards the other zones from Albania, i.e., to these other parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And can you elaborate on what supplies you're referring to. What kind of supplies are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about weapons supplies and other technical equipment that is needed to conduct a war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Can you tell us what specific steps were taken or discussed at this meeting to ensure that there was adequate co-ordination in terms of the supply of weapons through the Dukagjin zone?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'll object to the question. It assumes facts not in evidence. It calls for speculation. Discuss how the plan was, but the use of the word "ensure" presupposes that such a thing occurred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Menon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the witness was -- he was at the meeting, he indicates that "we wanted to co-ordinate the passage towards the other zones" -- excuse me -- yeah, he indicates the "Dukagjin zone had the responsibility to welcome these supplies ..." so he's talking about supplies, he's talking about the fact that they transited through this particular zone. I'm simply asking to elaborate whether there were any steps to ensure that that was effected. Surely if he was at the meeting he can either say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The objection is overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, he's changed his question. If he's asking whether steps were taken, he can ask yes or no. That's different. But he said: Can you tell us what specific steps, specific is in the context of this particular question also leading, and what it does is it suggests something, specific steps to ensure. Now, if his answer is yes or no, can you tell us what was done? Yes, I can; no, I can't. I'm in your hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Objection overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us whether at this particular meeting in mid-July 1998 in Jabllanice, whether there were any steps taken to ensure that supplies of weapons were adequately transited through the Dukagjin zone?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I recall correctly, we agreed and work started in this direction, i.e., to ensure the transiting of weapons through the operative zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: But can you elaborate on what -- on what, if any, steps were taken, what responsibilities were -- what responsibilities were given to the individual participants in this meeting to ensure that there was adequate transiting of weapons through the zone?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The details I cannot remember because a long time has elapsed since then, but these are the main elements of what was discussed at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Very well. If we could move on to - staying on the same exhibit - move on to page 213 in e-court, lines -- and I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Direct Your Honours' attention to lines 14 through 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Now, sir, in your prior testimony you indicated that when you visited Jabllanice in mid-July 1998 you visited certain units in Jabllanice. Can you tell us, sir, who accompanied you on these visits?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I visited Jabllanice after the meeting of the General Staff and the staffs from the operative zones, alongside me when inspecting those units was Salih Veseli and if I remember correctly at the time Driton Zeneli as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, do you recall who these men, Salih Veseli and Driton Zeneli, whom they reported to at the time?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Salih Veseli and Driton Zeneli reported to the commander of the zone, Ramush Haradinaj, at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. I'd like to move on to another topic, sir. Can you tell us whether you've ever met a person named Faton Mehmetaj?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have met him but I cannot recall the meetings. I think I met him in July or in August.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, can you tell us where you've met him, where you've -- the first time you met him, where did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I think I met him in Gllogjan at the command of the zone. He was based at a house there, but I can't remember exactly where.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And can you tell us, sir, at the time that you met him did he have an official position within the KLA staff of the Dukagjin zone?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I met him, he was assistant commander regarding intelligence, intelligence and counter-intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And can you tell us, sir, given that position as assistant commander regarding intelligence and counter-intelligence, what his functions would have been?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know what position he had before, but at that time he was assistant commander for intelligence and counter-intelligence and their duty was to gather information about the enemy and those pieces of information had to be passed on to the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And can you tell us, sir, whom he would have reported to at the time?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I was there, he reported to the commander of the operative zone of Dukagjin, Mr. Ramush Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And can you tell us, sir, when you first met him, who introduced you to Mr. Faton Mehmetaj?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, Salih Veseli was together with me at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And can you tell us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, just -- are you saying, sir, that Salih Veseli is the one who introduced you to him? To say you were together with him doesn't say that he introduced him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Salih Veseli was with me when I met Faton Mehmetaj for the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, the question is: Who introduced you to Faton Mehmetaj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I remember, it was Salih Veseli who introduced me to Faton Mehmetaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Menon. Yes, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, I just want, if I may, to ask you some general questions to give the Trial Chamber a flavour of the degree of real organisation that was in operation on the ground. I'm not asking you to answer that yet. I'm just indicating the topics on which I'm going to put some questions to you. First of all, you, I think, had some military experience; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And do you remember roughly when it was you were asked to join the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I joined in June 1998, as an officer at the operations department of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the General Staff had been in existence for how long -- so let me put that in the form of a clearer question to translate. How long had the General Staff been in existence before you were asked to join?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know for how long he had been in existence, but it was long before I joined it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you talking about the same thing?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think it's a mistranslation. It's "it" rather than "he."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, was the General Staff in existence, let us say, in January 1998?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I knew that it existed as a central staff at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In January 1998 you're saying you knew it was already in existence?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the information I had. I was not there at the time, but according to the information I received from Rexhep Selimi, the General Staff already existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And do you know from that information that you received whether it already existed, for example, in June of 1997, just so that we can confine the period?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, when -- when we talk about the General Staff, let's just perhaps help the Chamber what the reality of that was. First of all, the members of the General Staff that you had dealings with, were they based in Albania?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The members of the General Staff at the time were part of them in Albania but some of them were also in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I was careful in my question. The members of the General Staff that you yourself had dealings with directly, were they in Albania?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ones I had dealings with in 1998, in early 1998, in March and April, yes, they were in Albania, the ones I had contact with.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Because you didn't -- you say you had contact with them in March and April, but you didn't join the General Staff until June; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: At the time you joined the General Staff, did you know the names of the other members of the General Staff that were inside Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In Kosovo, when I arrived there, I got to know the other members of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so that we're clear, did the General Staff at this period of time, let us say from January till June, when you joined, did the General Staff have a premises at all from which to operate or did they meet in one another's flats?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are talking about Kosovo, within Kosovo, the staff was not based in one place and they had to move around because of various activities, operations. When I went there in June, that was the time when I met the staff for the first time and they were at the time in Likovc, but they used to move to different place, sometimes in Dukagjin, Berisha mountains, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's the General Staff members in Kosovo. I'm asking you about the General Staff in Albania. Did they have a premises or did they just meet in cafes and in people's flats?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, in Albania there was not a premises for the General Staff. The members of the staff that I met at the time, we usually used to meet in various flats. And as I said, the members of the staff that I used to meet there, we met in different flats or in various places outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it's right, isn't it, Mr. Zyrapi, that you even at that time didn't know who all the other members of the General Staff inside Albania were?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't know all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So does it follow you never met together as a composed General Staff at any time at that point? You didn't have meetings, regular meetings, as a full General Staff?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't, not in Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So basically you'd meet in groups of twos and threes; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you weren't -- you weren't properly constituted in any sense, were you, as a General Staff, as you understand that from your experience in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, you should remember, I was not a member of the staff yet, but according to my experience the staff should have the premises and they need to meet regularly and take decisions about the war or operations and how to go on with their work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I might just interrupt, Mr. Emmerson, when you say "at that time," can you just give us the date, month and year. What do you mean "at that time," which time are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I responded to the counsel's question and he asked me about the time in Albania. I was not a member then, and this was the period March, April, May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What year, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. I'm sorry to do that to you, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I'm grateful to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But can we be clear, Mr. Zyrapi, the reality is, dealing with the time-period, all the way through 1998 up to and including September I'm asking you now, I'm going to put some general propositions to you now, up to and including September 1998, first of all, I suggest to you throughout that period the General Staff never had regular meetings?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In Albania or anywhere.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained the situation in Albania. There were no meetings there and I was not a member.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But in Kosovo --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, just let me pause. I don't know whether you heard the introduction to my question, but I'm now asking you to deal with the period right the way through to September 1998. Because obviously we have your testimony from the last trial. In the last trial you told the Trial Chamber that from the period right up to September 1998 there were no regular meetings. Is that right? Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Menon.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, let me just understand the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: If we could have the transcript references if Mr. Emmerson refers to the last trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'll give you a series of transcript references: T-3279, T-3281, 3291, 3292, 3293, 3299.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And I would also ask that the witness's exact testimony be put to him rather than Mr. Emmerson paraphrasing.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me put a question to the witness if it troubles Mr. Menon.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is it right, Mr. Zyrapi, I'm suggesting this to you that throughout the period up to September 1998 there was, first of all, no General Staff premises in Albania; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There were no regular meetings of the General Staff in Albania; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The witness says as far as I know because I wonder if he is able to know for the period before he was a member.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He's already told us that the period before he was a member, as far as he can tell, there were none.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But from the period even after you were a member, Mr. Zyrapi, there were no regular meetings, were there, up to September 1998?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no regular meetings. There were some meetings where not all the members of the General Staff were present.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Even during that period, there were people who were members of the General Staff who you didn't know their names, weren't there, even in the period up to 1998, September 1998?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so, what we're really looking at is a group of men meeting in twos and threes and fours in flats and cafes without any formal operational structure in place throughout the period up to September 1998; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are talking about meetings in Albania where part of the staff was, but as I said, in June and July some members of the staff were in Likovc, in the mountains of Berisha. But as I said, this is only part of the staff. The other part of it was based in Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, and my question was: Right up until September 1998, so that we have the picture, the General Staff within Albania was meeting in twos and threes in flats and cafes; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes, but I don't know what other meetings they held.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, the people whom you say were members of the General Staff inside Kosovo, they were not based in one place either, were they?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The members of the staff that were inside Kosovo were placed in -- were based in different places, this for security reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So they never met together either, did they, during this period of time?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that in July we met. There was a large number of us meeting then and then there was another meeting in August, but these were not frequent meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And communication as well between those individuals who you say were floating inside of Kosovo and the members of the General Staff who were inside Albania, the communications were very poor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the time the communication was very poor. It was either direct, personal communication, or through radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And focusing now on --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Through courier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Can we just have a clarification as to which time-period that last answer related to.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I think the transcript is clear. The witness is talking about two meetings, one in July and one in August, and on the basis of that I'm asking him whether during the period, which we've been discussing, which is right up to September 1998 -- let me put it again to avoid any doubt.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The question, just for clarification, Mr. Zyrapi, is this: I'm suggesting to you that communications were very poor between those members of the General Staff inside Kosovo and those in Albania right up to and including September 1998. That's fair, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, communications were very poor at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just -- if we can then just stand back and summarise the position right up to and including September 1998, there were members -- and even after you yourself were a member, there were people who were calling themselves members of the General Staff inside Albania who you didn't know; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't meet all of them. The ones I had contact with, they told me they were members of the General Staff. I don't know who other -- who were the other people that were members of the same staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And at that time, between June and September 1998, was anybody -- when you first joined initially, was anybody able to tell you who were the members of the General Staff inside Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in July when I took the post at the operations department, Rexhep Selimi introduced me to the members of the General Staff. He told me the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so that we understand the position, did any other members of the General Staff have military experience, apart from you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the members of the General Staff there were no other people with military experience or educated as soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So this body calling itself the General Staff that had been in existence for at least six months before you joined it contained no one with any military background, had no premises, had no regular meetings, and met in groups of twos and three that couldn't communicate with the field in Kosovo. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was like that at the time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, if we can then turn to what was going on on the ground inside Kosovo. It's right, isn't it, that following the Serbian offensive in Gllogjan on the 24th of March, there was a greater willingness of the population and a general view amongst the Kosovar Albanian population that war was inevitable?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally, from March when the attack on the Jashari family occurred, then there was open war between us and the army and police forces of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But if we go back to the time when that occurred, let us say the beginning of March so that the Trial Chamber have it clear, there were two military operations, were there not, in March, one against the Jashari family compound and then on the 24th of March against the Haradinaj family compound in Gllogjan; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, and -- but if we go back to that period of time when those attacks occurred, there was no substantial Kosovo Liberation Army in existence, was there? I mean, we were dealing at that point in time with just a handful of individuals?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say about March, April, and May, but in June and July there were small groups self-organised that were carrying out defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So by the time we get to March, April, and May, you say there were self-organised groups. Now, let me just explore what you mean by "self-organised." Is it right to say that villages throughout Kosovo would one way or another try to put in place whatever they could to protect themselves, first of all?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. There were several groups in various villages that were self organised and they were trying to protect their villages and their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And generally, is it right that either the village elder or the village mayor would come to be, by popular agreement, regarded as the commander of the village defences?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't speak about earlier times, but from June there were groups in the villages that were self organised. And according to the tradition in our villages, the elder of the village would be the head of such groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so we know that there - if I can be absolutely blunt about it, Mr. Zyrapi - there was nothing, you would agree, that was a functioning General Staff, you've already told us that I think, as you would understand it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I explained, I can't say that there was no General Staff in existence, but there was no proper co-ordination and no proper co-ordination between the staff and the operational zones as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I was going to come onto that in a moment. But just let's look at what was going on on the ground. You've told us village mayors effectively leading village defences. Very few people with uniforms, is that right, at that time?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very few of them had uniforms at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, at least initially, very few people had weapons before weapons began to come in across the border from Albania?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I mean, in fact, the position is, is it not, that under the Serbian authority in Kosovo, it was not easy for ethnic Albanians to possess weapons?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And we've heard, obviously, and there's no dispute about this, that an operation began to smuggle in weapons from Albania after the collapse of the Albanian government. But those weapons that very often came across, they were old, poor quality, some of them Second World War issue; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were such kinds of weapons as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so into this - if I can use this term without being rude - but into this chaos over this period that we're dealing with, attempts were being made at every level to try to impose some kind of order; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I mean, you can't have -- you can't have self-commanded village defences all over the place with no one co-ordinating anything and expect to protect the community against the Serbs, can you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that partly involved using titles that didn't really reflect what was going on on the ground, didn't it, giving people names and ranks that weren't a reality in any conventional military sense?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: All right. Let me put the question a different way, Mr. Zyrapi. You've told us that there was a group of men calling themselves the General Staff, but they were not a General Staff in reality as you understand that term; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a General Staff, it was formed out of a political party and the movement, popular movement for the liberation of Kosova, but at the time you cannot talk in a military sense about the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly. But similarly, in the last trial you were shown a document dated the 23rd of June, which is -- which was recorded as a KLA document from the Dukagjin zone, which gave people certain ranks. For example, a man called Muhamet Berisha was appointed chemical and biological defence co-ordinator. There was no chemical and biological capability within the KLA, was there?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, I think the question may have been lost in translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The KLA did not have the capability to use chemical or biological weapons, did they? They didn't have any chemical or biological weapons?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't. They didn't have the weapons or the capability to protect against these weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That was going to be my next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Menon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: If Mr. Emmerson could give us a reference to a document because he's referred to a document from the Dukagjin zone which was --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: -- shown to the witness at the last trial. If he could just give us an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's 65 ter 00141 and it was exhibited at the last trial. And indeed this witness -- presumably it's exhibited to this witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to be clear, to make sure your answer was clear, not only did the KLA not have any chemical or biological capacity themselves, but they also had no possibility to defend the population against chemical or biological weapons; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so that title, as the person militarily responsible for chemical and biological defence, is just a name, isn't it, to give the appearance that the organisation is coming together?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time we were distributing these titles, there was -- they were part of the development of this structure from a military point of view during this period, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, but they were also partly about morale, weren't they, giving the impression that all these disparate villages could find somehow some sort of structure to operate in, same as the use of the term "General Staff." Wasn't that the reality, Mr. Zyrapi? Trying to impose some order on the chaos.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a -- an attempt to introduce some order during that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But -- so we got a person responsible for chemical and biological defence. We've also got somebody charged with commanding an anti-armoured unit, in other words, anti-tank combat. Did the KLA have anti-tank weapons in the middle of 2008 or not -- I'm sorry, 1998, or not?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the middle of 1998, as far as I recall, there were some anti-tank weapons, but they were of a smaller calibre. However, there was no unit, no anti-tank unit, in existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And do you know where in Kosovo - because of course Kosovo is a very comparatively large area - do you know which region of Kosovo had anti-tank weapons and which did not, even small-calibre ones?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm referring to the period that I inspected, that is, from June 1998. Some zones did have small-calibre anti-tank weapons. I'm talking about rocket-launchers, hand-held anti-tank rocket-launchers; however, not in sufficient quantity to enable us to protect ourselves or to attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: All right. So we've got a bit of a picture on the ground, if I've got this correctly, that essentially the KLA operated as it was during this period, up to September 1998, first of all, as independent pockets; and then coming together in an attempt to form sort of structure that was cohesive. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the beginning it was not very well organised; however, from this period onwards until September and October there were more efforts to set up a purely military structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But let's be completely honest about this, Mr. Zyrapi, because it's important. It's no shame to admit that the KLA did not operate as an army at any time up to 1998 in a way that you would recognise as having conventional command structures, did it? I'm sorry, September 1998.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So we have to -- I mean, you would agree, would you, with me that the Trial Chamber would have to be very, very careful not to assume that a title that's given to somebody reflects any conventional military authority that would normally be associated with that title? You would agree with that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the period we're talking about, yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And can I come back to there being separate power bases. So we've heard about the Jashari family compound. Can you tell the Trial Chamber where that compound was located?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Jashari family compound was in the Drenice territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it's an incident of livid national memory that the Serbian forces mounted an operation against the Jashari family compound in which every living thing was killed at the beginning of March 1998; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But can we just look at the situation before that operation. So you had a family power base in Drenice around the Jashari family, but did you also have in western Kosovo a separate power base around the Haradinaj family in Gllogjan and yet another separate power base around the Brahimaj family in Jabllanice, three different family power bases within western Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Menon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: It doesn't appear that there's any foundation for that particular question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There doesn't need to be. It's a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Zyrapi --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, let's rule. Overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, there were three separate family power bases in western Kosovo, let us say, at the end of February: The Jasharis in Drenice; the Haradinajs in Gllogjan; and, quite separately, the Brahimajs in Jabllanice. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. But apart from these families there were other families which gave their own contribution.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I was going to say those are three, but there were other power bases in different parts of Kosovo also organised around families or clans, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Then can we just look at the position at the beginning of this period, at the beginning of March. It would be absurd, wouldn't it, to suggest that the Haradinajs had the power to tell the Jasharis what to do or what not to do? That would be absurd, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it would be absurd to suggest that the Brahimajs could tell the Jasharis what to do, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it would be absurd to suggest that the Brahimajs could tell the Haradinajs what to do or what not to do within their own compound?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Menon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: It's completely unclear to me on what basis the witness is in a position to answer these questions. What knowledge would allow him to respond to those particular questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But you object after he has answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Well, no, I'm objecting to the last question, Your Honour, and he has not answered that last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought you used the word in plural, questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I respond. This man is being called by the Prosecution as the military expert who joined the General Staff in June and is in a population to describe command structures within the Kosovo Liberation Army. Now, obviously as a person who joined in June he needed to know what the military position was that he was joining. So the suggestion that he's not in a position to argue about -- to give evidence about relative control or the existence or absence of command structures prior to then is absurd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Emmerson, you're now talking about family relations here, the Jasharis, the Brahimajs, and the Brahimajs. You have moved away from the question of command structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm just saying I don't think anybody needs to be an experienced military person to know what the relations are between various families and what the power bases might be if he lives in that area he can know that and be able to tell that. So what I'm saying is your response -- your answer doesn't respond to the objection. But I still say to Mr. Menon he's objecting after the horses have bolted.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But I think Your Honour's also indicated, I can develop it if it assists, that the objection would be overruled in any event because as a person inside Kosovo he's in a position to give evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can just clarify one thing, Mr. Emmerson indicated that the Prosecution is calling this witness as a military expert. That's not the case, he's being called as a fact witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Menon. I think that correction is taken on board.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry for that diversion, Mr. Zyrapi, we were going through the relationships between the military power bases that were associated with the main families in western Kosovo. And you've told us that it would be absurd to suggest that either the Brahimajs or the Haradinajs could tell the Jasharis what to do or what not to do inside their compound and you've told us that it would be absurd to suggest that the Brahimajs could tell the Haradinajs what to do or what not to do inside their compound. The last question, which is the obvious concomitant of the first three: It would be absurd, would it not, to suggest that the Haradinajs were in a position to tell the Brahimajs at that point in time what to do or what not to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's the same problem. There's no basis for that question being put to this particular witness. It's not clear to me how he can comment on that particular family tie that Mr. Emmerson is referring to, the Haradinaj-Brahimaj family tie.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sure the witness can tell us if he's not able to comment on that tie. Overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It would be absurd, wouldn't it, Mr. Zyrapi, to suggest that in March 1998 the Haradinaj family could impose their will or discipline on what was or was not done by the Brahimajs inside Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And just so that it's clear about the period that we're concerned with up to September 1998, you've told us about the General Staff, you've told us about what was going on on the ground, you've told us about attempts to create the impression of a structure of command. What I want to be clear about is - and it may be obvious from what you've already said but it's important that the Trial Chamber should understand this - the General Staff weren't issuing military directives to any of these separate groupings, were they? They weren't telling them how to engage in combat, they weren't issuing with them any kind of military orders or instructions at all during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm happy to wait for the next answer; however, I'm a bit confused by Mr. Zyrapi's answer to Mr. Emmerson's question from lines 5 to 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And also I note the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I think -- if I can just clarify that one point before we break.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, just so that we can be absolutely clear because I think there may have been a translation issue. We're back at the beginning of March now, of 1998, you've told us that the Brahimajs couldn't tell the Jasharis what to do; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I don't know because I wasn't there, but surely the experience would show that, yes, that would be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And similarly, the Haradinajs couldn't tell the Brahimajs what to do and what not to do inside their compound?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Objection. I mean, that calls for speculation. The witness said: "At that time I don't know because I wasn't there ..." So essentially what Mr. Emmerson is inviting the witness to do is to speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, I think that question has been asked and answered. What was confusing Mr. Guy-Smith was your question at lines 5 to 7 of page 32. It would be absurd, Mr. Zyrapi, to suggest in March 1998 the Haradinaj family could impose their will or discipline on what was or was not done by the Brahimajs inside Jabllanice. Now, I think if Mr. Guy-Smith is confused, he must get -- he will get himself cleared when he cross-examines.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So you --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- I think the confusion arises because the witness was agreeing with the proposition but it records on the transcript as a no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think that's not the question Mr. Guy-Smith was raising.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's precisely what I was raising.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You said you are confused by the question and not by the answer, Mr. Emmerson is saying you were confused by the answer but you are saying you were confused by the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I said I'm a bit confused by Mr. Zyrapi's answer at line 21: I'm a bit confused by Mr. Zyrapi's answer to Mr. Emmerson's question from lines 5 to 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Line 21 of what page, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Page 32.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, 32.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think the point is simply this, the witness was plainly answering no to the question about whether or not it was possible for one family to impose their will on another.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's certainly the way that it came out, but I think that because of the translation he appears to have answered no to the proposition that it was absurd to suggest that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps the question can be put to the witness instead of Mr. Emmerson testifying.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: All right. Let -- I think Mr. Menon was objecting to the question but let's put it to the witness one final time before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, I want to suggest to you that in March 1998 none of those three families had authority to impose their will on one another. That is correct, is it not?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't there at that period to be able to know, but experience would show that, yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would that be an opportune moment then? We will take a break and come back at quarter to 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson. May the witness please be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we please have on the screen P78.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, just before we do that, just so that the record is clear, what are your intentions with respect to 65 ter 00141? You're not tendering it?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just give me a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You used it to cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I'm going to return to it and I'm going to -- it's already an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it already --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm pretty -- Your Honour's referring to the minutes dealing with chemical and biological warfare. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not able to say what it is. All I know is it is 65 ter 00141.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Give me a moment. Can somebody help me, please, is that ... [Trial Chamber and Registrar confer].

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, that is already Exhibit P191 in this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we call up, please, P78. And if we can just enlarge the portion in the centre. If we can just go in a bit, please. That's perfect.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, before we look at this map, Mr. Zyrapi, let me just explain to you what it is. You've told us about the situation at the beginning of the year with different power bases and the relationships between them. This map was produced and is admitted in these proceedings by Rrustem Tetaj, who was the commander of one of the subzones, and reflects the establishment of subzones at a meeting on the 23rd of May. All right. So that we're clear what it is that you're looking at. And you can -- you're comfortable with the geography. Do you need my help to -- that's the main Pec-Decani road running down north to south. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The agreed evidence in this case is that on the 23rd of May at a meeting in Gllogjan, an agreement was made to establish these different village defences that you've described into four subzones. And you can see them numbered --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Menon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Can Mr. Emmerson be a little more specific when he refers to the agreed evidence in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's the evidence of their own witness Rrustem Tetaj which has been admitted by this Trial Chamber by agreement from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The testimony of Mr. Rrustem Tetaj. Mr. Rogers opened it if Mr. Menon was watching the opening.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So we have four subzones then created which were bringing together the different village defences that you've described. Do you understand what I'm saying, Mr. Zyrapi?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's so small, I can't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Does Your Honour need it enlarged further? We can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That would be very helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we enlarge it further, please. Okay. That's better still.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So if we can just, Mr. Zyrapi, first of all, just familiarise yourself. We've looked at the road running north to south. We can see now on our screen on the bottom left-hand side Junik. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so the Judges understand, the border ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So the Judges understand, the border between Kosovo and Albania would be on the west side of this map, is that correct, it would be to the west of this map?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you say it one more time. Where? The border?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The border between Kosovo and Albania would be off this map but to the west.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So Junik, lying as it does on the west side of the Pec to Decan road, Pec-Decan Road, Junik was close to the border; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So if the Judges are trying to understand the route by which weapons entered the country, they'd be coming on this map from left to right; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the area to the west of the main road there, that was an area where there was often very intense fighting, is that correct, close to the border?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: If we could have a time-period for that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: During the period up to September 1998. There was often intense fighting between --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Starting from ... ?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: January 1998 -- well, March 1998, March to September there was fighting intensively along that area close to the border, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the Serbs controlled that road throughout this period of time, did they not, that runs north to south on our map on the left-hand side, that was always under effective Serbian control apart from a few occasions when it was interrupted?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Can Mr. Emmerson be specific as to the road he's referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Three times now, Mr. Menon, if you've followed the evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The road that runs north to south on the left-hand side from Pec to Decan and beyond. That road was consistently under Serbian control over a few very brief interruptions. Is that right, Mr. Zyrapi?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The entire road?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: All of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Which made it very difficult to control or communicate -- I'll put the question more clearly. Which made it very difficult to co-ordinate between forces on the east of that side of the road and forces on the west; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think you in fact visited that area on the west of the main road in your July visit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in June, but in July 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I said July. And it was difficult, wasn't it, for you to get across the road. You had to travel by night; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did you have to do part of the journey on foot?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Why did you have to do part of the journey on foot and travel at night?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For security reasons and because the route we followed to go to Junik was controlled by the Serb forces, and we had to walk in order not to be seen by those forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So in real terms it was always going to be very difficult, wasn't it, to bring the forces of the KLA that were stationed on the west side of the road into an effective joint command with any forces on the east side of the road. That was always going to be a problem, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, going back to the map, we're now, as I said to you, on the 23rd of May. And the agreed evidence is that on the 23rd of May, four subzones were created. Subzone 1, which included Gllogjan; subzone 2, which included Irzniq; subzone 3 which included Gornja and Donja Luka and Dashinoc or Dasinovac as it appears in the Serbian; and subzone 4 which included Istniq, Prapaqan, and Strellc. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And as we can see clearly, Jabllanice appears to the east of subzone 3 and is not included within the subzone formation; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this map, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So this, presumably, then was the first rudimentary attempt to create a co-ordinated command; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you agree --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I put it -- I'm accepting the objection, putting it a different way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you agree that this was the first rudimentary attempt to establish a co-ordinated structure?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Objection. Again, it's unclear to me, Your Honour, on what basis this witness is in a position to comment on events in May 1998 in the Dukagjin zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm sure Mr. Menon has read the transcript of this witness's evidence from the previous trial, during which the Prosecution led him precisely through all of these documents and invited him to comment on them. So he is in a position to deal with it. Perhaps the witness can say. Obviously if he doesn't understand any part of it or if there's any part he wasn't at any point familiar with, he'll be in a position to tell us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Objection overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, we have agreed evidence, I underline agreed again for Mr. Menon's benefit, that these four subzones were established on the 23rd of May for the first time. In other words, it was the first attempt to create any kind of subzone command. And I'm simply inviting you to confirm the obvious, which is that this was the first rudimentary attempt to create a co-ordinated series of commands. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what occurred at the period. I can speak about the period from July onwards and I saw what the situation was at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Well, that's a fair answer. So what we can see, though, for sure is that Jabllanice was not in one of the original four subzones?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, objection. The witness has answered as to the -- the witness has indicated what the limits of his knowledge are. He's indicated that he cannot comment on the map based upon the fact that he was not present in the zone until July 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Menon, you are mis-characterising what the witness said. He never said he can't comment on the map. He said he can't comment about the time in May because he was not there. But the question that is being put to him is an obvious one. According to how this map stands and how the subzones are delineated, the question is: Does the witness accept, not that it is what he knows from previous knowledge, but looking at this map does he accept that Jabllanice is outside the zones. That's the question. For that, you are overruled, Mr. Menon.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well -- so, Mr. Zyrapi, it's a question that almost doesn't need asking and answering, but it's obvious that Jabllanice is outside the four subzones; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Virtually a rhetorical question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, let me leave it, because it's so obvious that it doesn't need putting on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, what I wanted to get from you, which is not obvious, is that it took you, didn't it, about two hours, is that right, to drive from Jabllanice to Gllogjan on the day of your visit?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly how long it took us, two hours or three hours, but I know that it took a long time to get from Jabllanice to Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to give the Judges a sense of the geography and the terrain. Now, I want to ask you, please, to look at a document that you've been shown before by the Prosecution but which is exhibited in this case as P177, which takes us on in the chronology. This is the end of May or the 23rd of May, rather, the map. The next document I want to take you to is the 8th of June. Now, if we can have the English translation on the right side of the screen, please. Now, the minutes, as they are, of this meeting -- did you ever see minutes like this at the time?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, no, I didn't see such minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you were asked by the Prosecution to look at a lot of contemporary minutes and to comment on them, weren't you, before your evidence in the last trial?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, this, we can see, is a staff meeting on the 8th of June within that structure of the subzones of Gllogjan, Gramaqel, Rastavica, Carrabreg, Decan, and other places. And can you see just beneath the second horizontal line that the aim of the meeting is the defence of the positions and their movement.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: First of all, as somebody who's been in a real army, would you expect to see minutes in handwriting like this as the only record of what's being considered? Would you expect them to be simply handwritten on a piece of paper like this or would you expect them to be properly typed up and produced if you were in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minutes of meetings in a normal army are kept and they should be typewritten. However, in the period we're talking about, in June/July, it was not possible to typewrite them so they were handwritten.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Because the resources just weren't there. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, if we can turn in the English translation to the next page, page 2; and in the Albanian original also I think also to page 2 -- sorry, it's -- just to be clear. Could we turn to page 3 of the Albanian, keeping page 2, because they don't coincide. I've lost it now. I'm looking for this for your benefit. And one more page over, please. There should be two further tram lines. There we are. Do you see the passage of text between those two lines? Yes? On the left-hand side, in the Albanian original, can you see two lines going across the page, horizontal lines?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just beneath the first line, do you see an entry which says: "RH," Ramush Haradinaj, "a new front has opened in Dujaka ..." Yes? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Dujaka is Jabllanice, is it not?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, have I mispronounced it, Duskaja, is that the correct pronunciation?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Duskaja is close to Jabllanice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which is Duskaja here?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Does the minute refer to Duskaja?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far I can see here, it says "new front in Dujaka." I can't see any Duskaja.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. I'll leave the document then. Perhaps we can just -- before leaving it, just as an example of the way in which requests were then being made to the staff meetings in the four subzones, we see that a new front has opened in Dujaka. And it goes on: "They are asking for people there. The requests for flour are being met, while those for officers are being reviewed." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, is Dujaka inside any one of those four subzones?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I saw in the map, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So this is a request from one of the villages in -- within the four subzones for the provision of support, military and food; correct?
