utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we move now to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just for my own edification, and may I apologise in advance for my poor pronunciation of the names. I see that the interlocutors are RH and somebody called Decan, if that's the correction pronunciation, but Decan then says: "We have moved from Decan to Carrabreg." Is Decan the name of both a human being and a place?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I can't give evidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, I would like to check it with the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Decan is the name of a town. There's a town called Decan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And could that name also be given to a human being?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. From what I can see here, it's the place where the staff of that village was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I give Your Honours a general steer on this. You'll see in a number of these minutes that sometimes speakers are not identified by name but by the place that they are representing because they are the representatives of the independent village defence of Decan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I would like to put a question to the witness as well. Just one moment. He said -- I can't find the exact place. But he said that he had from the map that Dujaka was in one of the four subzones. Mr. Witness, could you please elaborate on that. Did you see that name on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I saw it on the map that was shown to me earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Does Your Honour want to have the map displayed so that the witness can point it out?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we re-call, please, P78.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you help us as to where within those four subzones Dujaka is?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the map, Dujaka is in subzone 1 on the road from Gjakove to Decan. It's on the right of the road from Gjakove to Decan.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So it's not in subzone 1, in fact, at all, it's beneath it, is that right? It's the circled area outside of subzone 1?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So in fact, we need to qualify your last answer in relation to that minute. This was a request from an area outside of the four subzones for assistance to be sent to them; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to this map, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm very grateful for Your Honour's clarification because that's an important point. Can we now, please, call up P179. And in the English translation, please, on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, in fact, I'm going to ask -- this is -- well, first of all, we can just look at the document. This is a document headed: "Meeting of the Gllogjan staff." 13th of June, 1998. And we can see that, amongst other people, Ramush Haradinaj is present. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so we're now -- I'm doing this chronologically. We're now into the middle of June. If the Registry can bring up the following page in the Albanian but keep the existing page in the English. I'd like you to focus in, please, on -- you can focus in even further on the entry beginning HA and the following entry against RH. I think we can just -- I think for the assistance of the witness it would be good if we went in further and have HA -- exactly. Sorry, I just saw the area being marked, but it hasn't been enlarged. Oh, you can't enlarge it any further. Very well. In the English I'm looking, just bear with me, because -- this is a slightly different translation. If you look towards the -- if Your Honours look towards the bottom of the right-hand page, an HA and an RH. Do you see that? Perhaps that can be enlarged. And for you, Mr. Zyrapi, we're looking at the entry where on the left-hand side of the page the letters HA appear. Do you have that? Do you see that? So HA, and we can see from the list of attendees that that's somebody with the name H. Abazi. Do you know what part of the Dukagjin area H. Abazi represented or came from?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hajdin Abazi, when I went there in July, he was based at Reka e Keqe area, in the Reka e Keqe municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. We can see that Mr. Abazi is saying -- and he's from the area to the west of the main road, which you've already told us was difficult to consolidate. So may I make that clear in geography terms. I may have asked this question already, but, Mr. Zyrapi, the area to the west where Junik is where you've told us the intense fighting was, where it was hard to reach and you have to go by night and on foot, that is generally known as Reka e Keqe; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the Reka e Keqe area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so what we're seeing here is a representative from that side of the road, if I can put it that way, close to the border making a proposal. And the record of the minute says this: "From what I understand, the first step would be consolidation. The second is the creation of the subzone within the framework of the Dukagjini zone." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So am I correct in understanding that what is being suggested here is that in addition to those four subzones, a subzone covering Reka e Keqe should be joined on?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But it's right, isn't it, that there was no such suggestion, as far as you're aware, from Jabllanice at this time?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There was no such request, as far as you're aware, from Jabllanice at this time, to be joined on to the subzones?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know because I was not there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Well, we'll look at another minute in a minute which you've already been asked by the Prosecution to comment on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, before you go on, Mr. Emmerson, could you assist me. The -- your -- the way you -- and I don't know whether it is something which loses its significance with the translation, but your question to the witness - and he replied in the affirmative - was whether the subzone covering Reka e Keqe should be joined on. And then you asked you -- you contrasted that with the position of Jabllanice. What I'm wondering is whether you intended to say "could" or "should."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Perhaps if I can read the whole minutes I can pick up Your Honour's question and see if it should be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So the representative from Reka e Keqe is saying at this meeting: "From what I understand the first step would be consolidation. The second is the creation of the subzone within the framework of the Dukagjini Zone." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: To which RH replies after an unintelligible passage: "Is in favour of the co-ordination of single directing body. If we continue like this, with a multitude of staffs, it will be difficult." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And when you were shown this document before, you expressed the view - and I'm just inviting you to confirm that this is your view - that this document is consistent with what you knew to be the position, which was that local staffs were operating independently of one another.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think you are in a position to say this as well, are you not, that meetings of this kind were taking place all over Kosovo in an attempt to get these independently operating structures into some sort of co-ordination?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that happened in other areas as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't know if you know how asparagus grows, but it grows from an essential crown out of which there are maybe 20 or 30 spikes of asparagus penetrating up from the ground. I'm just asking you to take that on board first before I ask you the question. The reality at this time is that there were headquarters sprouted up all over Kosovo, all acting independently from one another, but with attempts being made to find some method of communication and co-ordination. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that's exactly what we see going on here, in these minutes?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, fast-forwarding to your visit to Reka e Keqe in July, so some weeks at least after this minute, would you agree that by then Reka e Keqe had still not been co-ordinated or brought within the subzone command, even in July?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember from my visit there at the time, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. So the fact that we see these -- the suggestions being made does not suggest for a moment that they've been effectively implemented straight away, does it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And this was a fledgling organisation, struggling to get on its feet, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And without effective direction of its operations from the General Staff, would you agree that the command structure, if there was one, was horizontal rather than vertical. To avoid the risk of mistranslation let me put the question in a shorter form. I'm suggesting to you that there was no vertical command structure in operation effectively on the ground at this time?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And all of these attempts to organise a structure were taking place under the barrage of constant Serbian attacks, weren't they, in all of these towns and villages?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so the Trial Chamber has the flavour, I mean, they would involve incursions by the Serbian forces on both sides of the road, in which everybody in a village would be killed and their crops and homes and livestock burnt?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And again, so the Trial Chamber has the picture, there were huge, very large numbers of very well-equipped Serbian military forces operating out of the area out of Decan, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Can we just have clarity as to the time-period.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The time-period up to September 1998, from January -- well, from March to September 1998. So I put the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Between March and September 1998, there were large numbers of Serbian military, military police, and paramilitaries, all very heavily equipped, conducting these attacks on Kosovar Albanian villages on both sides of the road; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the period from March to September, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And these villages were defended, as you've told us, by village guards without uniforms, with or without weapons doing their limited best to avoid massacres. Would you say that was fair?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, before the witness answers, it's a very broad question. Mr. Emmerson is referring to "these villages." It's unclear to me which specific villages he's referring to. Perhaps he could put the question to the witness a little more specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The villages under attack is the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: But which -- it's still not clear to me which specific villages he's referring to, which specific villages in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm making a rather more general point, but if Mr. Menon requires me to formulate it, I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, first of all, the Serbs attacked villages on both sides of the road, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During this period, yes, on both sides of the road villages came under attack from Serbian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: From Pec right down to Decani?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Peje to Decan and then from Decan to Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And they would penetrate into the territory on both sides of the road, killing everything that they found; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The attacks occurred in these territories and these attacks had their consequences, and I think that the KLA troops, to the best of their ability, tried to protect these villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And on top of the ground attacks, there was heavy artillery being used on areas where it was thought that the KLA were organising; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Shelling. Just to be clear, Mr. Zyrapi, and it may be an obvious point. Did those conditions make it easier or more difficult for this fledgling organisation to establish effective command and co-ordination?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This certainly made it more difficult, not only the attempts to organise but also to stay put.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we please bring up P191. This is the document I referred to earlier on which Your Honour asked me whether I was going to seek its admission?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You haven't forgotten Judge Hall's question? I thought it is -- it relates to this issue, whether it should be or could be incorporated or consolidated.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I thought I had moved on and dealt with it in a different way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you're happy with the answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I'm content, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think Your Honour will recall, we then -- the witness then testified that even though that's what was being proposed, weeks later when he went there it still hadn't happened. So it's perhaps "should" at the beginning and "could" at the end because it was an intention that could not, in fact, be put into effect. That's the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: By the time he visited in July. Can we now look at these minutes, please, for the 23rd of June --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, what is the --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exhibit number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is -- the Trial Chamber will have an opportunity to read and hear and consider other evidence about this meeting, but this is, I'm going to suggest to you as we look at it, another meeting to try to bring people together in some form of co-ordinated command. And you can see that those present include Ramush, Captain Rrustem Tetaj, and Maxhupi, and Nazmi Brahimaj, amongst a number of others. And the very first substantial entry is Mr. Haradinaj, recorded as follows: "R. Haradinaj: Explained the organisational structure of the areas of competence of the Staff of the Dukagjin area, so far divided up into six subzones. "The purpose of the meeting: Co-ordinating, participating, exchanging experiences, and organising a single command." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if we can just, please, look in the English translation, first of all, two pages further on for the heading "Rrustem Tetaj" beneath the horizontal line. I think we have this slight problem of inconsistent translation. Sorry, could we go back a page to page 2. Yes. And if you can just -- now, if we can find the corresponding passage, please, on the Albanian original. So we'll need to go through page by page, I'm afraid. Yes, I think that is it. So here on the 23rd of June, Mr. Tetaj, who is commander of subzone 2, whilst Mr. Haradinaj is commander of subzone 1, Mr. Tetaj is saying to all present: "It's a historic day. It's a large zone with large forces. I support my colleague. Let us determine tasks, let us," I'll slow down a bit, "let us settle the direction of work and co-ordinate it. Of course I am with Ramush who said that war is not only waged by defending posts. Let us rout the enemy at the posts where they are and make them feel insecure." And then Mr. Tetaj says this: "In my opinion: There has been little use of our forces. There is no excuse for self-satisfaction with what has been done. I cannot call our territory a free zone while the enemy holds the routes -- the road routes and towns. "In order to proceed, we need co-ordination, a single command. In order to go forward, I ... delighted about all the soldiers I see. Today is not time for ranks but only the time to fight the enemy." And then this: "We took a step forward when we formed the Dukagjin staff." Pausing there, and Mr. Tetaj has indicated that that's a reference to the 23rd of May and the map that you've seen. "The results have been evident. I mention Salih who came to help at the critical moment." And then: "We have now taken another step to lay the groundwork for preparing personnel, a military school." Now, pausing there for a moment, you can see that Mr. Tetaj is expressing the view that in order to be effective it is necessary for these different commanders to form some sort of single command in order to go forward, do you see that, some sort of co-ordinated command?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So can we take it, Mr. Zyrapi, that right up to the 23rd of June there was no such command in existence?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to these comments, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And now if we can just go to the end of the document, please, when ranks begin to be assigned. So that's the last page on the Albanian and it's the previous page, perhaps the bottom half of the previous page. So that we can see that at -- during the course of this meeting, as the whole of the minutes show, a decision was taken to try to establish one of these rudimentary command structures. And various roles are given to various people. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you've already told us that the different KLA power bases, Gllogjan and Jabllanice, began in March as being entirely independent of one another; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I don't think that the witness gave --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. I accept that. That's probably taking that -- the transcript's capable of being read. I take the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, we can see, as you've just told us in your last answer, that there was no co-ordination into a single command prior to this date, and we've seen from the map that Jabllanice is two hours' drive away from the existing subzones that had been formed. This is the meeting at which various ranks are assigned, including chemical and biological defence, the one at the bottom, and anti-armoured unit combat for Skenderi. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so this is the meeting about which you've already told us that often, in trying to put things together, names are given which don't reflect any military reality on the ground; correct? Names and ranks are given which do not reflect any practical military reality on the ground?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the document, it appears to be the case. Whether it was such in reality, I don't know. This document, however, shows it to be like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But it was the reality, wasn't it, even with the General Staff, people calling themselves a General Staff that were not a General Staff by any conventional military analysis?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it was a staff in the process of being formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. And so too was this, would you agree, an attempt --

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe the witness has answered that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't think he has.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: At lines 6 through 9 he's indicated what he knows about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm asking him, having read it, does he agree that this too was an attempt to create a staff that was in formation, just as the General Staff was. Does he accept that this too was?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I guess he answered that question at line 16 when you said, "yes, exactly."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, he was answering a question about the General Staff not being a General Staff in any conventional military sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm asking him whether he agrees that this staff, which is not a General Staff but the local staff, is in the same way allocating titles which are aspirational --

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, that question has been answered at lines 9 through 12, where the witness indicated: "According to the document, it appears to be the case. Whether it was such in reality, I don't know. This document, however, shows it to be like that." The witness has indicated what the extent of his knowledge is and what his ability to answer the question is. Objection. So I take an objection to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If it's not helpful to Your Honours, I'm not going to pursue it. Can I just indicate what exactly has happened in the questions and answers because if one follows them it's reasonably clear. The witness accepts that the General Staff was not a General Staff in any conventional sense. It called itself a General Staff because it was in the process of formation throughout this period. He also accepts that roles and responsibilities here, in the local staff, were being assigned in the Dukagjini zone in circumstances where Jabllanice and Gllogjan had never been in any joint staff priority the 23rd of June but a meeting is taking place at which names and titles are being dished out. And I'm asking him: From his consideration of this minute, which he's seen before, is it the case that, just as with the General Staff, titles are given to an organisation that's in the process of formation, so too in relation to this, it's an organisation -- a local organisation in the process of formation. That was the question. It may be too complicated, it may not assist Your Honours, the answer may be rather obvious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, and I think you asked that question -- I think I'm following you, at line 13 of page 59, but it was the reality, wasn't it, even with the General Staff, people calling themselves a General Staff that were not a General Staff by any conventional military analysis. And the question -- the answer is: Yes, but it was a staff in the process of being formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And you -- that's exactly what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: As soon as you said that you said exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't know whether we're talking at cross-purposes, but is that analysis also applicable to the Dukagjini regional staff as evidenced in these minutes. This is not a General Staff meeting, it is a first meeting in an attempt to bring together two wholly independent power bases on this witness's evidence and is that therefore in the process of formation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: To the extent that you are saying it doesn't refer to the General Staff but to this --

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I add something, I do believe, actually, that Mr. Emmerson has put that particular question as it relates to the Dukagjin zone to the witness and I refer Your Honours to lines 6 through 9 on page 59 where he -- the witness is obviously being shown the document and Mr. Emmerson asks whether the names and ranks that are given whether they reflect any practical military reality on the ground and the witness says: "According to the document it appears to be the case. Whether it was such in reality, I don't know. This document, however, shows it to be like that." So the witness has indicated what information he can give concerning the ranks that existed within the Dukagjin zone in the specific time-period of this document. He's indicated how much information he can give.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me put the question to you this way, Mr. Zyrapi. When you got there in July --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm just going -- not going to argue endlessly here. The material is obvious from the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When you got there in July, Mr. Zyrapi, you saw what was going on across the zone isn't it true that the reality is that these structures were still in the process of formation?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, during the month of July when I visited, they were in the process of formation, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you're introduced to Ramush Haradinaj as the man who's been recently elected as the zone commander, but that does not imply, does it, operational effective control on the ground throughout the Dukagjin zone at that time?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for the time we're speaking about, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, you agree with what I said?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. So you met Mr. Haradinaj at Jabllanice because Jabllanice was the first stop on your trip; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He came there to meet you, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We [Realtime transcript read in error "he"] came from the General Staff with the other members, and we met at Jabllanice where we found Mr. Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, but you knew, didn't you, that Mr. Haradinaj was based in Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So he'd come over there to meet you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So whatever the position on paper, the practical reality on the ground was that Mr. Haradinaj was the commander over in Gllogjan, but others were in command in Jabllanice. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know prior to that, but in July when I went to visit Jabllanice was under the command of the operational zone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's something that concerns me here that's not clear to me, and I need assistance from the witness. Mr. Zyrapi, you were asked: "So you met Mr. Haradinaj at Jabllanice because Jabllanice was the first stop on your trip; is that right?" You said: "Yes." I need to understand the meaning of the word "met" in context. Met as if introduced -- seeing him for the first time and being introduced or you had a meeting -- you are going to meet there, did you have an appointment to meet there as people who know each other already?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Me alongside a number of General Staff members had certain appointment at Jabllanice between the General Staff and the command of the Dukagjin operational zone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, that suffices.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour - I'm sorry to interrupt, Mr. Emmerson - but there was another answer immediately following that which I think has been erroneously recorded in the transcript and it could be important. He came there to meet you, didn't he? The answer: No, he came from the General Staff. I heard the witness say "we" and I think that probably does need to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. Thank you very much for that. He said we came from the General Staff and Mr. Haradinaj obviously came from his base in Gllogjan, and that's where they met, in the sense of coinciding.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You took a tour around Jabllanice when you arrived, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived at Jabllanice, I visited the village of Jabllanice, I mean the positions as they existed in Jabllanice where the KLA units were.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you visited each of the -- each of the areas you were shown as military facilities in Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I inspected the positions, the place where KLA units were positioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you've already told us that you know that Mr. Haradinaj was based in Gllogjan. Were you with him when you toured the military facilities in Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I visited alongside Salih Veseli and Driton.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you were visiting as a senior person in this fledgling structure, coming to look at the facility; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't a matter of premises. I'm talking about the front lines, the positions occupied by the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, you didn't see, did you, anything that looked to you at the time of your visit to be a detention facility or a prison where people were being detained?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As I mentioned it, I visited the front lines as well as the house where the General Staff held its meeting with the commander of the operational zone. I did not visit any other physical premises.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You were not, as a result of your visit -- nobody suggested to you, you were not aware, that there was a detention facility there? Nothing struck you or you didn't see or hear anything that caused you to believe that there was a detention facility or that people were being detained there at the time of your visit?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not informed of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, so that we're clear, just in terms of command, on the command issue alone this is the last but one topic I'm going to touch on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it a whole topic?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it a topic or just a question?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is one question and then I've got one more.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we were to take the theoretical position of commands as they were emerging, you would be in command of Ramush Haradinaj, wouldn't you, if we're to take what's written on paper as real, you would be his commander, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, just a follow-up question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Follow-up question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The follow-up question is this: I'm not suggesting anything untoward did occur at Jabllanice, that's for other witnesses and other moments. But if anything had happened there regarded as criminal, would you regard yourself as responsible for that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If I have no information of that and if I was not present.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we rise, may the witness be excused. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I noticed that one of your team members by repetition after you put a question nodded slightly. I'm sure it doesn't mean anything, but it is disturbing.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I understand. I'm sure we will all bear that in mind. Sometimes these things happen involuntarily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sure whoever it was, it was an involuntary response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We'll all be aware.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll take a break and come back at half past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you continue, Mr. Emmerson, can I just raise the point which has been reported to us. And what I'm going to talk about didn't happen the last session but it might have happened in the morning session. There is a request from the translation section that we try not to overlap when we speak, and I know that at times emotions go a little high and we get a little agitated. I have been directed also to that. So can we be sure we give one enough a chance to speak so the record can be -- the interpreters are having difficulty with that problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson -- oh, Mr. Guy-Smith is on his feet. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm on my feet because Mr. Emmerson said that he had no further questions, and I was waiting for guidance from the Court to proceed, which is why I got on my feet because I didn't want all of us sitting here wondering what was going to happen next.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh, I have been remiss. Did you say you have finished your questions, Mr. Emmerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might, Mr. Zyrapi, with regard to the questions and answers you have given thus far, I'd like to focus on a couple of locations and a couple of times if I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And could we have P78 up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And as I understand your testimony, between the periods of March and September there was intense fighting on both sides of the road, the Pec-Decani road, and that during that period of time there were Serb invasions or incursions to villages on both sides of the road. And it's with that in mind that I'm going to be asking you the following questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we have the map enlarged a little bit around the area of Junik, please. And perhaps if it could be just a little bit bigger just to make sure we all can see because I -- yes, thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, I notice on the map - and this would be towards Albania - a placed called Pobrdje. Do you see that on the map?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you tell us at the time that you were visiting the area, first of all, whether or not that particular area, Pobrdje, is geographically higher than the region around it.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see from the -- second around the Junik area -- side the Junik area. It is a higher area than Junik -- which is a bit higher --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, we're having a bit of a problem. We're hearing two interpreters -- or is it only me?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm getting --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm getting two.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm getting feedback, but I'm so used to that at this point, so I don't know whether it's me or the machines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It didn't sound like feedback, but it sounded like two separate voices, a male and a female.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, let's see what we can do about that because I want to make sure that we're dealing with a single-gender response in translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, try again.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Surely.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to the area around Pobrdje, do you recall that that area was under the control of the Serbs and was used as a place for shelling? By that I mean they shelled the villages around the area from that position.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The place where this Serb artillery was positioned was called Kodri i Geshtenjave and it's close to the village of Pobrdje.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Perhaps if it's of some assistance to the Chamber, are you in a position to mark on this map where Kodri i Geshtenjave is and I'd ask the usher for some assistance. And for purposes of this exercise, I don't know what colour you are going to be using, perhaps it would be good to use the colour blue, as I've been told there are other colours other than the colour red available to us.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will mark it approximately where it was, this place.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I can't be exact now. Here, in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say "here, in this area," that is the station of the artillery that was used by the Serbian forces for purposes of shelling; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you do us the kindness, since you're there, of putting a line under the village of Pobrdje, just a single blue line?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And with regard to the map once again, do you see the village of Voksh on the map?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And could you put a blue circle around the village of Voksh, indicating where it is located?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And just for purposes of clarity, because one of the things that often occurs at later times when people are reading transcripts, could you mark the first circle, that is, the area of Kodri i Geshtenjave with an A for artillery. Just put an A right by where you made the first marking so that we have a reference point of where the Serbian artillery was placed.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, were you aware of the fact that Mr. Balaj and his unit, the Black Eagles, were in Voksh in the month of June, as reflected in the letter that you discussed with the Prosecutor in P162?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of that at the time, but according to the letter I was shown, the letter showed that he was there in the village of Voksh.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And we will come back to the letter, but I've been told that you can't move anything on the screen. So before we go any further what I'd also like to do so we can do this in one complete session with regard to the map is you have told us also that you met Idriz Balaj, who is known to you as Toger, when you went on your visit in mid-July in Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you circle on the map where Irzniq is, please.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And could you put a T next to that to indicate the place where you met Toger.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I have that admitted as a Defence next in order or first in order, and I don't know what the designation is that Mr. Registrar is using for those purposes. Because it's -- because it's a -- it was P78. Now that I've put markings on it I've got to re --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure. Just before we do that, I just wanted to find out from the witness if you do know, Mr. Zyrapi, how long Mr. Balaj was for in the first village where you met him - was it in June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I went there, it was mid-July, and I only stayed with him about 10 to 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, my question is: Do you know how long he was in that village for in -- is it Kodri I Geshtenjave?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Kodri i Geshtenjave, Your Honours, is the place where the Serbian artillery --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And you said he was with his unit where?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Voksh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Voksh. Do you know how long Mr. Balaj was in Voksh for, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And in Irzniq do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how long he had been in Irzniq, but when I visited Irzniq in July he was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Mr. Registrar, will you please give an exhibit number to this as a Defence exhibit. It's admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, marked -- map marked in the court by the witness shall be -- it's Exhibit P78 shall be assigned Exhibit D144. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I ask again for guidance. The first time in the Tribunal we handled -- or I have been involved in a trial of more than one accused. Do we need to make a distinction between the Defence attorneys whose exhibit this is?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We did not at the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- at the initial trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I don't think from what I understand we are going to do it this time either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. The Defence -- what is the exhibit number, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's D144.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Sorry for interrupting you, Mr. Guy-Smith. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Not a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you met Mr. Balaj in mid-July in Irzniq, you learned at that time that he was the head of a rapid intervention unit; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you also learned at that time that the place where he and his unit were billeted was near a school, about a hundred to 150 metres away from a school in Irzniq; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, with regard -- and now I'm going to go back to a time before you met Mr. Balaj. With regard to the month of June, are you aware of the fact that Mr. Balaj was in Voksh fighting during that month with his unit?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you receive any information with regard to members of the Black Eagles who were killed, and specifically that on June 3rd in Pobrdje Altin Haskaj was killed during battle and Rexhep Thaqi. Was wounded?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think I had that information at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Have you become aware of that information since that time?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, now yes. But at the time I didn't know. I was not there to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand that. And with regard to the date of June 14th at the time, once again, were you aware that Armend Kukleqi and Blerim Lokaj were killed, also members of Mr. Balaj's Black Eagle unit during combat?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that would have been in Drenoc?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know then.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I take it, similarly, you were not aware at the time that Valmir Ukaj had been wounded as a result of his involvement in combat under Idriz Balaj's command as -- in the Black Eagles?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Since that time have you become aware of the fact that Armend Kukleqi and Blerim Lokaj were killed during combat operations and Valmir Ukaj was wounded during fighting in the rapid intervention unit of the Toger?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I didn't. Later on, yes, I heard about all of these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to these deaths and these woundings, could you tell us whether or not these deaths and these woundings occurred while the Serbian forces were, as you have previously told us, engaged in heavy conflict on both sides of the road, attempting to enter and destroy villages?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there was fighting at that time, however, I was not informed about these killings and the people who were wounded at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Subsequent to these battles, did you learn of this -- did you learn of these killings and of these woundings?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: After that time?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was much later. It was not during that period. Even in July when I went there, I did not have information about these events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, I'm sorry, it's not very well with me. Please listen to the question. The question is after the time, after you had been in this area, did you come to know of the deaths and injury of these people that are mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I explained that in June, July, August when I visited, I did not know about the killings and the woundings. I knew that there had been fighting in the territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, you are still not answering the question. I'm going to try and say it one more time. It is understood that during June, July, and August when you visited there you did not know. The question is: After August, wherever you might have been, did you come to know of these deaths and injuries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Later I was informed that people had been killed and wounded, but I didn't know the names and surnames. I was not informed about the names of the people who were killed. Later on, much later, I learned the names of the people who were killed, after the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That approximates an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That approximates an answer, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I want to go back to the map which has now been admitted as D144 and ask you another question. You were speaking with Mr. Emmerson about the issue of formation, and could you tell me just this, Irzniq is in subzone 2; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as the map shows.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And could you -- you'd mentioned earlier that the time that it took to get from Gllogjan to Jabllanice was two hours. And would that be approximately the same period of time to get from Irzniq to Jabllanice? Or would it be longer or shorter as a result of the roads?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The time it took for us to get from Gllogjan to Jabllanice was what I mentioned, and I think that from Irzniq to Jabllanice it takes approximately the same amount of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to getting from Voksh to Jabllanice, which requires, as I understand, among other things, travelling by foot, travelling at night, and avoiding the Serbian forces that controlled the main road, could you tell us how long a period of time it would take under optimal conditions to get from Voksh to Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never measured the time. However, to go to Voksh at the time you would have to go through territories that were under Serbian control, so you couldn't go there during day-time. And I would assume that it would take much longer to get from Voksh to Jabllanice.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say it would take much longer to get to Voksh from Jabllanice, considering the factors that you have told us about, can you give us any reasonable estimate of the time that it would take?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult to give an exact time because it would depend on the situation and how able you were to pass -- to go through Serbian positions. Everything was done at night and we tried -- it had to be done quickly from Jabllanice to Gllogjan and then from Gllogjan to Voksh, it could take four or five hours depending on the situation and where the Serbs were exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Taking that into account - and as I said to you before, given an optimal period of time, meaning that you had free sailing, it was a period that you did not have to either wait or fight with the Serbs, can you tell us how long that would take? Can you approximate it for us?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the witness has given an answer, he was asked initially at lines 22 to 23, can you give us any reasonable estimate of the time it would take and he gave his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Except in that I was not quite clear in my mind whether the four to five hours relates from the strip to Gllogjan to Voksh or from Jabllanice to Voksh so --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let me try to break it down then. We have a period of two to three hours from Gllogjan to Jabllanice --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, but I would like to hear from the witness what the four to five hours relates to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I was going to ask him with regard to travelling from Voksh area or the Irzniq area to Voksh or back, from Voksh to Gllogjan or Irzniq, what period of time would that take?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I travelled through those areas, from Gllogjan to Junik, it was about four hours, from Gllogjan to Junik. And from Junik to Voksh you would need another hour or two. So overall you would have five to six hours depending on the situation pertaining at the time. From Jabllanice the time would be much, much longer. It could be from seven, eight, ten hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think we have an answer. And could I please have P162 up on the screen. First of all, could you tell us what the date is of this particular document.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document in front of me dates -- has the date of the 3rd of July 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I'd like you to look down in the document and it starts off -- there's a line that starts off with "Voksh is ..." do you see that, particular line that says "Voksh is" and then goes on "grateful."

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to this particular language here: "Voksh is grateful to the KLA special unit led by Togeri because were it not for this fighter and his hinds, the village of Voksh would today be in the hands of the Serbo-Slav-chauvinist enemy."

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's what I can read.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know what happened after the Black Eagles left Voksh?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Could you tell us whether or not in your experience you have seen such commendations being made by other individuals or villages for the efforts and protecting a particular village such as Voksh?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Attempts to defend villages were carried out all over the territory, and the Rapid Reaction Force was created especially for that purpose, to help these villages as well as the units tasked with protecting the villages, i.e., to reinforce them. That was the main task of the units of the rapid intervention force.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I understand your answer, would it be fair to say where there was trouble, where the Serbs were attacking, the Black Eagles went? That was their purpose.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tasks of the Rapid Reaction Force were to go to the aid of the villages and the fronts that came under attack by the Serbian forces to help them protect their villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Guy-Smith. Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I think I'm going to need that podium again, if you would just give me a second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You can take two.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Zyrapi.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And I think you know that I have the honour to represent Lahi Brahimaj in these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, may I just ask you about your first arrival inside Kosovo. I believe you entered the country on the 28th of May of 1998; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you went straight to the headquarters of the General Staff which at that stage would have been in Likovc; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the first time - and I entered on the 28th of May - I stopped at the village of Drenoc in the Rahovec municipality, where I stayed for a few days. From there we proceeded to Likovc, where a part of the General Staff was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't mean to suggest you could get there all in one day. It was obviously difficulty travelling, as you've already told us, travelling at night-time and having to stay in people's houses and be very, very careful where you were at all times.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I see you nodding. When you got there, therefore, we're talking about early June, probably the first week in June, would that be right, 1998?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And I -- obviously you can't remember everybody you would have met on your first day or two there, but would I be right in saying that Rexhep Selimi was there and introduced you to other members of the General Staff who were already inside the country?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Rexhep Selimi and Hashim Thaqi who were with us introduced us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Correct. Rexhep Selimi, Hashim Thaqi, and was Jakup Krasniqi there at that stage as well?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jakup Krasniqi was there too, as was Sokol Bashota, people who I met -- amongst the people I met at Likovc.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And do you remember also that Lahi Brahimaj was there on that occasion as well?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Are you saying you remember that he wasn't there or you simply can't remember whether he was there on that occasion or not?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I recall, I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you stay for a long time in Likovc or did you go off and -- to other parts of the -- of Kosovo at that time?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed for a brief period of time, after which I was appointed in the operational director as the man in charge for the development of the KLA, after which I went to inspect the different areas, and primarily the Drenice one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Again, I don't expect you to be precise, but how quickly did you leave for Drenice, within two or three days?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Likovc staff was located in the territory of the operational zone of Drenice. I cannot recall exactly how long I stayed, was it two days or three days, I don't know, but it was a very brief period; after which, pursuant to the orders issued by the operational commander at the time, Rexhep Selimi, I was tasked with a duty to go to the operational zone of Drenice in order to render my advice for the development of the operational zone of Drenice.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And so you spent some time in Drenice and which was the next operational zone you went to after you had given your advice to the people of Drenice?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that I moved on to the Pashtrik Operational Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And approximately how long do you think you spent in the Pashtrik Zone?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall exactly, but in both the Drenice and the Pashtrik Operational Zone, I visited them in July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Do we understand that you would go to a zone like Pashtrik and simply stay there for a period of time, or would you come back and forth and spend some nights in -- with the other members of the General Staff and other nights you'd be on the road or in the zone?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I mean staying, I mean staying with the local units in the positions where they were and where I was giving my military advice. I wasn't moving to and fro and, i.e., from the zone to the staff headquarters, and I'm referring to this period, from June to the beginning of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if I suggest to you that you, in fact, did meet Lahi Brahimaj in your first days in early June of 1998 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, objection. I think the witness has answered the question as to whether or not he's met --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I haven't asked the question yet. I simply asked him whether he met him on his first day there. The witness said he did not remember. I think I'm entitled to pursue that. I have not put in terms to him when, on instructions, I say he first met with my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So as I was just about to ask you, Mr. Zyrapi, do you recall -- sorry. If I suggest this to you, that you, in fact, did meet Mr. Brahimaj in your early days in June before you went off to Pashtrik or around Drenice, may that be correct? Can you rule out the possibility that in fact you did meet him then?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember to have met him during that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's not the question, Mr. Zyrapi. The question is: Would you dispute that you met him is the question. That you remember or don't remember is one thing, but are you in a position to dispute meeting him if it's put to you that you did meet him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't confirm or deny it because I cannot remember it for the time-period we're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: That's all I'm asking. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I then want to come to the period when you were working with Lahi for some time at the General Staff, weren't you, and you would see him very frequently over a period of time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And his duties were in -- to be in charge of finance and logistics, procurement of weapons?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, he was director of finances at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if Mr. Harvey could clarify what time he's referring to. It's unclear. Because the previous question obviously related to -- the earlier questions related to early June, so it's unclear whether we're referring to a different time-period now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any response, Mr. Harvey?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I was about to ask that question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Will you proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection now, Mr. Zyrapi, can you recall was that around the early to the middle part of July that you were working with him on a regular basis?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first part of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you. And the term "General Staff," Main Staff," "central staff," all of these terms have been used. Are we talking about the same body of people?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The General Staff or the central staff is one and the same. We are talking about the same people.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And some people use the term "Main Staff." Is that the same as well?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And there is no question -- am I right, there is no question, Lahi Brahimaj was indeed a member of the General Staff, the central staff, the Main Staff, whatever we call it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from July when I was there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And I appreciate, you're not in a position to say when he first took up his position on the General Staff because you weren't aware of who was on the General Staff before you arrived yourself?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you. And now dealing with when you travelled from Drenice to the Dukagjin Zone. Lahi accompanied you together with Hashim Thaqi and Jakup Krasniqi; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And again, there's no question in your mind, Lahi Brahimaj was accompanying you in his capacity as a member of the General Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You understood that his family home was in Jabllanice; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And did you understand also that at some earlier stage he had been one of the commanders in that area?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to the information that was given to me by the former operational commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And the former operational commander you mean who?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the operational department of the General Staff headed by Rexhep Selimi.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Rexhep Selimi had told you that Lahi Brahimaj was previously one of the commanders in the Jabllanice area of the Dukagjin Zone?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: When you went with Lahi to Jabllanice, you went to his family home there, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we went to Jabllanice, we stayed in the family home of Lahi Brahimaj. That's where we had the meeting between the General Staff and the commander of the Dukagjin Operational Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Do you recall how long the journey took you because you were walking and travelling by night, I believe you told us, how long did it take you to get from Drenice to Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall exactly, but it took very long because of having to go through security areas. It did take quite a long time, but I cannot say how long.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Were you able to accomplish the journey in one night or did you have to stop somewhere along the way?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We travelled through the night. In fact, we set off at midnight from the staff headquarters, and at dawn the next day we reached Jabllanice.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And did you happen to pass through areas that were under the control of the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were some areas controlled by Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You had the meeting in Lahi's family home, and what happened then? Did you leave straight away with Mr. Haradinaj to go to Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the meeting and, in fact, as I said even in the course of the meeting, I inspected units at Jabllanice, after which I went to Gllogjan command centre alongside Mr. Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And when you say that you inspected units at Jabllanice, you went to more than one place in Jabllanice to inspect those units; yes?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as I said earlier, I went to the front lines where the positions of the KLA units were, meaning around Jabllanice.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And I think you have, at least on a previous occasion if not here today, you said that the person who took you was the commander at Jabllanice, and his name was Driton Zeneli. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I inspected these units there was Salih Veseli and Driton. They were all present when I went to inspect these positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And which of them did you understand to be the commander at Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I think it was told to me that Driton was the commander of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And if my learned friends want a transcript reference for that, it's at page 3388, Exhibit 159. When you went together with Ramush towards Gllogjan, did Lahi remain behind in Jabllanice or do you know what he did?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember, but I know that after leaving I went to Gllogjan. Whether he stayed or returned in the company of the other staff members, I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And I think the next you heard from Mr. Brahimaj was when you received a message that you had to return urgently to Jabllanice in order to accompany him to Rahovec, where there was a Serb attack underway; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And was it your understanding that Lahi Brahimaj had brought that message from the General Staff, summoning you both back to Rahovec?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The message was to go from the operational zone of Dukagjin to Rahovec, where the General Staff was concentrated, as a result of the fighting around the Rahovec municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And it was Lahi who had brought that message to Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Lahi brought the message, and in his own car he took me to the Rahovec municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I just want to clear up a couple of points in your statement that's exhibited as P160. Perhaps it would help if we had that on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I clear one point --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- which I don't understand. As I understood the evidence, the witness left Jabllanice with Mr. Ramush Haradinaj going to Gllogjan and he doesn't know whether -- what happened to Mr. Brahimaj while he was -- when he left. Now, you then asked the question, Mr. Harvey, that -- saying Mr. -- I'm trying to find this place. Give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I think I know what's troubling Your Honour. I asked him if Mr. Brahimaj had brought the message from the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] --.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: To Jabllanice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Exactly. And I thought he was in Gllogjan with Mr. Ramush Haradinaj at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No, let me clarify that with the witness if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, am I correct in understanding you. Lahi Brahimaj did not accompany you to Gllogjan with Ramush Haradinaj; am I right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And I think you told Their Honours that you left and you don't know whether Lahi returned to Drenice with the other members of the General Staff or whether he remained in Jabllanice; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: But you were summoned to go quickly to Jabllanice; yes?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two days later I was summoned to go to Jabllanice, and then from there to Rahovec.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And when you got to Jabllanice, there was Lahi Brahimaj with a message from the General Staff, saying: Both of you, get to Rahovec as quickly as possible, and you set off in his car?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I got to Jabllanice, Lahi told me that fighting had started in Rahovec and we needed to go to Rahovec at the order of the General Staff. And then we together went from Jabllanice to Rahovec.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And am I right in assuming you don't know one way or the other whether Lahi Brahimaj had physically brought that order from Drenice or from Rahovec or whether he'd received it by some other means?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Does that clear up matters, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, thanks. Thank you so much, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, I'd asked if your statement at P160. Could we go to paragraph 16 of that statement, please, page 4. Yes, if we could just enlarge -- oh.
