We seem to have a redacted version of it there. I'm comfortable with paragraph 16 at least. In fact, I see we've already clarified the only issue of substance there, and it's really the blanked-out paragraph 18 that I wanted -- can we go over the page to paragraph 19. I think that's the only matter that's really significant left to deal with. No, we can't. Oh. Very well. Well, in that case I'm going to have to read what I have because I assume that Your Honours do have the unredacted statement. Am I wrong about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Would Your Honours just give me a moment because I don't want to be cross-examining something in that should be out. Would you give me a moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure. Consider also in the light that there are redactions do we need to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, since this is not a matter before this Court, I don't need to waste anyone's time with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Let me just ask you this in conclusion, Mr. Zyrapi. You were in Jabllanice second time I think towards the end of August/beginning of September; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And on that occasion did you also inspect units in that region?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And in inspecting units and meeting with the soldiers, presumably, you received reports of what was happening generally in that region in and around Jabllanice; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Can you remember whether you talked to soldiers in Jabllanice itself?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my visit to the front lines and the unit commanders and the soldiers, I talked with them, but I can't remember the details of those conversations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I wasn't going to question you about the details of conversations. I'm more concerned with where you went to. Did you meet with soldiers in Jabllanice itself?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In some of the positions where I went to inspect, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And do you recall going to inspect any of the soldiers' quarters, see where they lived in Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think I did at the time. I did go to the front line and the commanders of the units, but not where the soldiers were staying.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: At any time, both on your first visit to Jabllanice and on that second visit, at any time did anyone tell you, did you hear from any of those soldiers any suggestion that people were being detained against their will in Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, both the first time and the second time when I went to Jabllanice, I never heard such complaints.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Harvey. Mr. Menon, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Yes, just a few questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us in the period from March to mid -- excuse me, in the period from March to the end of May 1998 where you were based?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From March to May 1998, I was based in Tirana.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And prior to March 1998, where were you, sir?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before March 1998 I was living in the Netherlands with my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, when you were referred to Tirana, do I take that that that's in Albania?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Tirana is the capital of Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, from the end of May or from the beginning of June until July 1998, sir, where were you based?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From June to July 1998 - I think I mentioned this earlier - in the beginning when I entered Kosovo I stayed in Drenoc near Rahovec and then in Likovc in the territory of Drenice and then I moved around in the areas of Drenice and Pashtrik. I did not have a static base, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And let's take the period from the July to September 1998. What about that period? Where were you in that period?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the attacks on Rahovec in July and then the rest of the Serbian offensive, I was moving around in Rahovec, Pashtrik, Drenice, Shala, these were the places where I was staying from July to September. In September I left Kosovo, went to Albania, and then from Albania into Kosovo back later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, can you tell us when -- when you first met Mr. Ramush Haradinaj, in which month and year?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time I met him was in April in Tirana, when he came to the flat where I was staying with some colleagues, other officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And can you --

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and Mr. Ramush Haradinaj came there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I'm sorry for having interrupted you there, sir. Can you tell us how long your encounter with Ramush Haradinaj on that occasion lasted?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time I met him I don't think it was more than three or four minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, when was the next time that you met Mr. Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next time was when we met in mid-July, and that was the time when we went to have the meeting between the General Staff and the operational zone commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And if we could pull up Exhibit P159 and go to page 42 in e-court. And, sir, I'm going to read from the transcript here. You were asked, and this is from the previous trial: "Do you know Lahi Brahimaj?" And you said: "Yes." And then you were asked: "Can you tell the Trial Chamber when you first met him?" And you indicated: "For the first time? I saw him in July in the General Staff." Sir, do you adopt that answer now?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I say "in July," yes, I stand by it because that was the time when I saw him and then the contacts between us continued in the framework of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. Sir, I want to take you back to an answer that you gave earlier today to Mr. Emmerson. It was put to you that in the period from March to September 1998 you had indicated that on both sides of the Pec to Decani/Decani to Djakovica road, that on both sides of that road villages had come under attack from Serb forces, sir, in the period from March to September 1998. How did you acquire that information, sir?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This information I received when I visited the Dukagjin area, the first time and the second time, while the rest of the information was given to me by the director of the operations department, Mr. Rexhep Selimi.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And do you know how Mr. Rexhep Selimi would have acquired the information, sir?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether at the time he was present in the area himself or what other ways he could have had to gain that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, if we could pull up Exhibit P133. Your Honour, if I could just have a minute. This is not the correct exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How long are you going to be with the witness on this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I needed another perhaps ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We are at the end of the day. We can't go for ten minutes. Maybe -- would you like to maybe deal with that next time?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Yes, I mean it would be -- it would be unfortunate to keep the witness over the weekend, but I do have another ten minutes of re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Another ten minutes of re-examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. -- you need ten minutes to finish your re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I would estimate, based upon the answers -- obviously it depends on the answers the witness gives and whether they require clarification, but I would say 10 to 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We can't give you that much, Mr. Menon. I'm sorry, we will have to adjourn to next week. There are other commitments that are calling on us this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry about that. Sorry, Mr. Zyrapi, we haven't finished with you. It's unfortunate that you have to stay the weekend here, but that's how things go. You are now being excused until Monday afternoon, I think it is. We sit in the afternoon, same courtroom, quarter past 2.00, but I -- don't take your headphones yet. I've got to warn you that you are still under oath, you are still in the witness box, you may not discuss the case with anybody, in particular not with the Prosecution whose witness you are. We'll see you on Monday at quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon. You are excused. You may leave the courtroom until Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I can give you one minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, then I won't say a word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's all right. We have to adjourn, I'm sorry, to Monday, quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon, same courtroom. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 29th day of August, 2011, at 2.15 p.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
